example.paragraph_en: Bacteria are everywhere. They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets. In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear. They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe. And it only takes a little bit of dirt to damage your timber floors. The more dirt you track in, the more it scratches and the more often you'd have to clean. The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time. Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointed or hard parts. These can dent and scratch your floor. And if you live in an apartment building, removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors.

example.paragraph_en: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency. Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to. Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier. If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.
example.paragraph_zh: 尽管把所有假期都用来享受一次漫长的暑假可能很有吸引力，但你的总体目标应该是在假期长度、愉悦感和休假频率之间取得完美平衡。休假频率很重要，因为在全年安排多次休息意味着你总有值得期待的事情。筹划事情以及随之而来的期待往往会让我们更加快乐。如果你每年只休一次长假，兴奋感会积累得慢得多，而且由于假期看起来遥不可及，实际上可能会让人产生绝望感。

example.paragraph_en: Another science-based reason to focus on one thing at a time is that when you begin practising a new habit, it requires a lot of conscious effort to remember to do it. After a while, however, the pattern of behavior becomes easier. Eventually, your new habit becomes a normal routine, and the process is more or less mindless and automatic. The time it takes to build a habit depends on many factors, including how difficult the habit is, your genetics, and more.

example.paragraph_en: There are scenarios in which forgiveness is not the best course. Sometimes the victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive. Forgiveness can be challenging. This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all. However, it's often the healthiest path forward. It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender, reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life.
example.paragraph_zh: 在某些情况下，宽恕并不是最佳选择。有时，当受害者允许自己不去宽恕时，他们反而会获得更强的力量。宽恕可能是一件困难的事。当冒犯者给出虚假的道歉，或者根本没有道歉时，尤其如此。然而，宽恕往往是最有利于健康的前进之路。重要的是，要通过对冒犯者培养同情心来促进宽恕，并反思这一行为究竟是出于恶意，还是由冒犯者生活中的艰难处境所导致。

example.paragraph_en: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed. example.paragraph_en: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency. example.paragraph_en: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite. But that was all before newspapers, television and the internet. In today's hyper connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe. Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are. Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events by definition aren't news.
example.paragraph_zh: 在我们的进化史中，我们的注意力很容易被负面信息吸引是一件非常有益的事，因为这些信息很可能意味着对自身生存构成的危险。那个总是假定下一块岩石后面有一头狮子的穴居人通常会判断错误，但与总是假定情况相反的人相比，他存活并繁衍后代的可能性要大得多。但那是在报纸、电视和互联网出现以前。如今，在这个高度互联的时代，我们对坏消息的沉迷只会让我们从全球各地吸纳令人沮丧或愤怒的故事。无论这些新闻是否真的对我们构成威胁，我们都会得出这样的结论：事情比实际情况糟糕得多。另一方面，真正的好消息在报纸上往往更难被发现，因为可预见的日常事件按定义来说并不算新闻。

example.paragraph_en: Whole grain foods will ward off hunger. Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread. Combining whole grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration. Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack. Blueberries, like many dark colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age-related decline. Frozen berries are also a good choice. They are usually cheap, last longer and don't lose their nutrients when frozen. But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.

example.paragraph_en: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors. They found that if pollution is frozen to around –18 °C in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through. Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants. It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.

example.text: This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."
example.zh: 这项针对世界各地60种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有群体都遵循七项基本的道德准则。这些普遍规则是：帮助家人，帮助群体，回报他人的帮助，勇敢，服从上级，公平分配资源，以及尊重他人的财产。研究人员发现，无论是传统的狩猎采集者群体，还是先进文明，各类社会都重视这些品格；这些品格有助于维护文明社会并促进社会合作。“每个地方的每个人都拥有共同的道德准则，”牛津大学首席作者兼高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·柯里博士说，“这七条道德规则之所以在不同文化中都具有普遍性，是因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。即便其中一些品格看起来属于右翼或保守立场，例如服从权威，左翼人士仍然会表现出对某个群体的忠诚，以及对某个人或某种事物的服从。这表明，真正将我们联结在一起的因素多于分裂我们的因素。”

example.paragraph_en: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes. Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others. The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found. "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford. "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems. Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."

example.paragraph_en: Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat? Do you find other cities to be more or less polite? Different cities have different feels for visitors. Some are friendly and open; some are formal and distant. Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude. That's what some tourists have said. One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities. Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn and occasionally cursing at each other. Drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park, but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.
example.paragraph_zh: 你认为波士顿人会铺上迎宾垫吗？你觉得其他城市的人更有礼貌，还是不那么有礼貌？不同的城市给游客的感觉各不相同。有些城市友好而开放，有些则拘谨而疏远。波士顿往往给人一种行色匆匆、有时还有些粗鲁的感觉。一些游客就是这么说的。一项研究发现，这里的人主动自愿帮助陌生人的意愿低于美国其他城市的居民。下次你在波士顿时，不妨仔细看看，你很可能会看到以下一些情景：尽管地铁站经常提醒人们不要吸烟，还是有人在那里吸烟；人行横道信号灯显示禁止通行时，行人仍然无视汽车继续行走；汽车司机超速行驶，大声按喇叭，偶尔还互相破口大骂。有些司机懒得找停车位，反而只是打开转向灯，把车停在马路中央。

example.text: Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others.
example.zh: 这项针对世界各地60种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有群体都遵循七项基本的道德准则。这些普遍规则是：帮助家人，帮助群体，回报他人的帮助，勇敢，服从上级，公平分配资源，以及尊重他人的财产。研究人员发现，无论是传统的狩猎采集者群体，还是先进文明，各类社会都重视这些品格；这些品格有助于维护文明社会并促进社会合作。“每个地方的每个人都拥有共同的道德准则，”牛津大学首席作者兼高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·柯里博士说，“这七条道德规则之所以在不同文化中都具有普遍性，是因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。即便其中一些品格看起来属于右翼或保守立场，例如服从权威，左翼人士仍然会表现出对某个群体的忠诚，以及对某个人或某种事物的服从。这表明，真正将我们联结在一起的因素多于分裂我们的因素。”

example.paragraph_en: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes. Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others. The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found. "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford. "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems. Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."

example.paragraph_en: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business. The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington, D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B. On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you. Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family. You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved. The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.

example.paragraph_en: If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you'd realise if it had changed your beliefs? No one knows your own mind like you do—it seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted. And yet a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article.
example.paragraph_zh: 如果你读了一篇有关争议性问题的文章，你认为自己会意识到它是否改变了你的信念吗？没有人比你更了解自己的想法——你似乎理所当然会知道自己的信念是否发生了变化。然而，《实验心理学季刊》发表的一篇新论文表明，我们实际上很难觉察到自己的信念变化，这意味着我们往往会低估自己受一篇有说服力的文章影响的程度。

example.paragraph_en: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite. But that was all before newspapers, television and the internet. In today's hyper connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe. Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are. Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events by definition aren't news.
example.paragraph_zh: 在我们的进化史中，我们的注意力很容易被负面信息吸引是一件非常有益的事，因为这些信息很可能意味着对自身生存构成的危险。那个总是假定下一块岩石后面有一头狮子的穴居人通常会判断错误，但与总是假定情况相反的人相比，他存活并繁衍后代的可能性要大得多。但那是在报纸、电视和互联网出现以前。如今，在这个高度互联的时代，我们对坏消息的沉迷只会让我们从全球各地吸纳令人沮丧或愤怒的故事。无论这些新闻是否真的对我们构成威胁，我们都会得出这样的结论：事情比实际情况糟糕得多。另一方面，真正的好消息在报纸上往往更难被发现，因为可预见的日常事件按定义来说并不算新闻。

example.paragraph_zh: 在YouGov于2015年进行的一项调查中，65%的英国人和81%的法国人表示，他们认为世界正在变得越来越糟。然而，根据大量合理的统计数据，这些人的看法显然是错误的。任何心智正常的人都不应希望自己生活在过去的某个世纪。然而，人们确实会有这样的愿望。为什么？

example.paragraph_en: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts. These strategies are learned in childhood. Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations. We just do whatever seems to come naturally. But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts. When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person. How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict. Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.

example.paragraph_en: A pattern in nature is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors. Some of the most striking examples include the six-sided arrays of rocks at Giant's Causeway in the United Kingdom, and the colorful stripes and spots on tropical fish. Patterns like these begin to form at a small scale when materials undergo processes like drying, freezing, wrinkling, diffusing and reacting. Those changes then give rise to complex patterns at a larger scale that people can see.
example.paragraph_zh: 自然界中的图案，是指形状或颜色有规律地重复排列的任何形式。其中一些最引人注目的例子包括英国巨人之路上六边形的岩石阵列，以及热带鱼身上色彩斑斓的条纹和斑点。这类图案在材料经历干燥、冻结、起皱、扩散和反应等过程时，会先在微小尺度上开始形成。随后，这些变化会在更大尺度上产生人们能够看见的复杂图案。

example.paragraph_en: To anyone thinking about becoming a travel writer, I would suggest they first try and look for a unique way to enter the industry. example.paragraph_en: But let's be real. Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not. Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children. As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids. But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives. Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.

example.paragraph_en: Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world.
